title: A depth-one quotient of a regular local surface has principal kernel
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak n)$ be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of Krull dimension $2$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $I\subseteq\mathfrak n$ be an ideal. If the local ring $A/I$ has depth $1$ [def-weil-pbc-depth], then there exists a nonzero $f\in\mathfrak n$ such that $I=(f)$.

proof.text: Because a regular system of parameters of A has length 2 and is a regular sequence, while the depth of every nonzero finite module is at most the dimension of its support, depth(A)=2. Hence I cannot be zero: if I=0 then A/I=A would have depth 2, contrary to the depth-one hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0C48, proof of part (2), opening reduction I != 0; depth definitions and the regular-local parameter sequence are supplied by the cited nodes.

proof.text: Since A is Noetherian, choose a finite generating list f_1,...,f_r of the nonzero ideal I. The regular-local UFD statement [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization] gives a nonzero common gcd f and elements g_i with f_i=f g_i, where the g_i have no common nonunit divisor. Thus I=fJ for J=(g_1,...,g_r).

source.place: Tag 0C48, proof of part (2), paragraph beginning 'Assume I not = 0. Write I=(f_1,...,f_r)' and the gcd factorization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-coprime-generators-mprimary-or-unit] to the residual generators. If J=A, then I=fJ=(f), and f is nonzero and lies in n, giving the conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0C48, proof of part (2), the sentence 'Then either (g_1,...,g_r)=A which implies I=(f)'.

proof.text: It remains to treat the case sqrt(J)=n. The class z of f in M=A/I is annihilated by every g_i, hence J is contained in Ann_A(z). If z were nonzero, the cyclic submodule P=Az (isomorphic to A/Ann_A(z)) would be finite and its support would have the unique minimal prime n, because the radical of Ann_A(z) is n. The minimal-support associated-prime theorem gives n in Ass_A(P), and the associated-prime inclusion for a submodule P -> M gives n in Ass_A(M). But depth(M)=1 means that n is not associated: otherwise every element of n would be a zerodivisor on M, so no nonempty M-regular sequence in n could exist. Therefore z=0, so f belongs to I; since I=fJ, this yields I=(f).

source.place: Tag 0C48, proof of part (2), final paragraph: depth one excludes the maximal associated prime, so the class of f annihilated by the residual generators is zero.

The item states it exactly: regular local, Krull dimension 2, I in n, depth(A/I)=1, giving I=(f) with f nonzero and in n. Nothing is weakened. Step 1: n has 2 generators, which form a regular sequence (lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence), so depth A>=2 and I=0 is ruled out. Step 2: the UFD node gives the gcd extraction I=fJ in a few lines. Step 3: the case J=A gives I=(f). Step 4: J kills the class z of f. If z were nonzero, Supp(Az)={n}, so n is in Ass(Az) by the minimal-support Mathlib leaf and in Ass(A/I) by the exact-sequence node. Then every element of n is a zerodivisor on A/I, which contradicts depth 1. So f is in I. All hypotheses were checked where used. Item tested on F[[u,v]] with I=0, n, (u^2,uv), (u), (uv), (u^2-v^3). lean.statement: theorem regularSurfaceDepthOnePrincipal (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsRegularLocalRing A] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = (2 : WithBot ℕ∞)) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I ≤ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) (hdepth : letI : Nontrivial (A ⧸ I) := Ideal.Quotient.nontrivial_iff.mpr (ne_top_of_le_ne_top (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal.isMaximal A).ne_top hI) letI : IsLocalRing (A ⧸ I) := IsLocalRing.of_surjective' (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective IsLocalRing.depth (R := A ⧸ I) (A ⧸ I) = (1 : ℕ∞)) : ∃ f : A, f ≠ 0 ∧ f ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A ∧ I = Ideal.span {f}
